# jochwacht-sbom 0.20.0 — reads your Yocto and Buildroot build directory, names the release

**Security fix:** up to 0.19.0 the collector followed a symbolic link when it
wrote its files into the scanned folder: `sbom.cdx.json` and the diagnosis
file `jochwacht-sbom-diagnosis.json` since 0.12.0, and in 0.19.0 also
`.jochwacht/last-upload.json` and the folder `.jochwacht` itself. A scanned
repository you do not control, such as a pull request from a fork in CI, could
make it write outside that folder. 0.20.0 writes none of its files through a
link: it refuses with a message, and the diagnosis file goes to the temporary
directory under a fresh name, which the run names. Please update; see the
security advisory of this repository.

**Security fix: `go list` runs offline.** From 0.18.0 to 0.19.0 the default
run called `go list` with go's own network settings when a Go toolchain was
installed: modules missing from your module cache were downloaded from the Go
module proxy (their names and versions left your machine), and a `go` or
`toolchain` line in `go.mod` could make go download and run another Go
toolchain. 0.20.0 runs the default run's `go list` offline (`GOPROXY=off`,
`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, no checksum database, no direct VCS access, `go.mod`
never rewritten) over your own settings. When something is missing, the run
says so and lists `go.sum` instead; `go mod download` fills the cache. See the
second security advisory of this repository.

**`--with-tools` runs the project's own build code** (cmake runs the
`CMakeLists.txt`, Gradle the project's `gradlew`, Conan the `conanfile.py`,
Maven its plugins), and these tools use the network. Use it only on code you
trust, never on a pull request from a fork. The help text and the README now
say so; the cmake trace runs in a temporary folder outside the scanned folder.

- **A Yocto or Buildroot build directory in the scanned path is read.** Run
  the tool on the folder that holds `build/` or `output/`: the local bill
  carries what the build proves (the delivered packages, their files, the
  image files, the creator, the product the build states). The upload stays
  as slim as in 0.19: names, versions and your own declarations; the build
  evidence stays on your machine.
- A build part linked out of the scanned folder is named and never read. One
  broken build is recorded as a gap; the healthy ones stay in the bill.
  Reader warnings reach the summary.
- Yocto image files are found by poky's naming, kirkstone included.
- The source tree of an in-tree Buildroot build is not scanned as your product.
- **`--release` names the release of the version you send** (or
  `JOCHWACHT_RELEASE`, at most 100 characters, never shortened). Without it
  the collector takes the git tag exactly on the current commit, else the
  product version your Buildroot or Yocto build states, when it is yours and
  not the tool's default. The output names where the label came from; without
  one, nothing is sent.
- **In CI, name the release with `--release`** in the pipeline (for example
  your tag). The derived label comes from the scanned content and is meant
  for work on your own machine.
- `--send --yes` names the copy that was uploaded
  (`.jochwacht/sent.cdx.json`) and whether the release gets a full check or
  watch only.
- The product can be named in UTF-8; the refusals of the server (unknown or
  blocked key, a key limited to other products, release label missing or
  invalid) get clear sentences, and server text is cleaned at the source.
- One licence library with the Jochwacht suite; `NOASSERTION` and similar are
  no licence.
